item.title: Common Ground Book Club: books by & about people with disabilities — Fri Nov 6, 10:30 AM — Sebastopol Library
item.description:
Meet with others to discuss books centering disability voices! Copies of each month's books are available at the Sonoma County Library Catalog. Pre-Register to receive a reminder email. Drop-ins are welcome. If you didn't have time to read or finish the month's book, you are still welcome to attend. Snacks will be provided. Common Ground Society serves families who have loved ones with any sort of unique need while also educating our community on how to be inclusive. Held the 1st Friday of the month from 10:30-11:30am. We will not be meeting in January. 12/05/2025- December's title is Unfit Parent : A Disabled Mother Challenges An Inaccessible World by Jessica Slice 2/06/2025- Disability Intimacy: Essays on Love, Care, and Desire: Edited by Alice Wong 3/06/2025- The Kiss Quotient by Helen Hoang 04/03/2025- True Biz by Sara Nović 05/01/2025- Second Life: Having a Child in the Digital Age by Amanda Hess
Source: North Bay Bohemian

item.title: Scanning - Playback Memory Lab — Fri Nov 6, 1:00 PM — Sonoma County History & Genealogy Library
item.description:
Register for a 3-hour appointment to digitize your documents and photos, slides and negatives. Appointments are available Thursdays, Fridays, and Saturdays, 1-4pm. Limited to 1 station per day, 1 appointment per week, per library card holder. The Memory Lab user who books the lab appointment must have a Sonoma County Library general card account, be age 18 or older, and read and agree to the User Agreement online. By clicking "Register" on this event, the Lab User agrees to follow the terms and conditions in the attached User Agreement. For more information: If you need Spanish-language assistance for your first visit, please contact staff.

item.title: Healthcare Forum 2026 + Resource Fair — Fri Nov 13, 10:30 AM — The Backdrop @ Becoming Independent
item.description:
Healthcare Forum 2026 & Resource Fair
Tickets Are On Sale Now!
Last November, almost 300 people showed up for "What's Changing in Healthcare and What To Do Next," our Healthcare Forum & Resource Fair. The atmosphere was unbelievable.
Regional experts, healthcare providers, and community leaders came together to cut through the noise and connect Sonoma County families with real healthcare resources.

More details on speakers and the program are coming soon.

item.title: Paint & Sip with Genevieve Elkin — Fri Nov 13, 5:30 PM — Petaluma Arts Center
item.description:
Join us for a relaxed and social paint & sip evening. You'll be guided step-by-step through painting a scenic view using acrylics, with plenty of room to make it your own.
Whether you follow along or add your own creative twist, the focus is on enjoying the process and having fun. Sip on a beverage, come with friends or meet new ones, and settle into a laid-back night of painting and connection. No experience needed - just show up and create.
Genevieve Elkin was Born and raised in Mill Valley, California and is a multidisciplinary artist now based in Petaluma. She earned a BFA in Illustration from Parsons School of Design and has professionally managed art departments, supporting artists and new media on high-profile projects. Genevieve loves painting, drawing, and exploring ceramics, and enjoys helping students experiment, have fun, and develop their own creative voice.
To learn more:@gennaelkin

item.title: Write & Collage: Words, Images & Memory — Sat Nov 14, 10:00 AM — Petaluma Arts Center
item.description:
Join Marlene Cullen for a creative two-hour experience that brings writing and collage together. In the first hour, guided freewriting prompts invite you to explore memorable moments, stories, and experiences in a welcoming, supportive environment. In the second hour, transform those reflections into a visual expression using images, colors, and textures.
No writing or art experience is necessary—just bring your curiosity and a willingness to explore.
Bring: A notebook and pen. Collage materials will be provided, and you're welcome to bring a favorite poem, magazines, photographs, or other materials you'd like to incorporate.
Marlene Cullen is the founder of Writers Forum and creator of Jumpstart Writing Workshops. Through her website and blog, The Write Spot, she shares resources and inspiration to help writers discover and develop their voices.
The Write Spot anthologies edited by Marlene are collections of short stories, poems, and vignettes with prompts to encourage writing.
